registry_name: AutoLearn KT-RL Human Pilot Experiment Registry
project_title: Knowledge-Tracing-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Personalized Exercise Selection

study_design.type: Randomized Controlled Trial (RCT) with Parallel Arms
study_design.blinding: Double-blind (participants and teaching assistants blinded to policy allocation)
study_design.curriculum_domain: Introductory Python & Algorithm Design (52 items, 30 KCs)

study_arms.name: Prerequisite Difficulty Ladder (Standard Baseline)
study_arms.description: Standard sequential curriculum progressing from lower to higher difficulty upon prerequisite satisfaction

study_arms.name: Composite Adaptive Policy (Rule-Based KT)
study_arms.description: Combines BKT mastery, spacing decay, entropy uncertainty, and difficulty recovery hysteretic state machine

study_arms.name: Dueling Double DQN Policy (Deep RL)
study_arms.description: 99-dimensional state space policy selecting exercises to maximize cumulative multi-objective pedagogical reward

study_arms.name: LinUCB Contextual Bandit Policy
study_arms.description: Upper Confidence Bound contextual linear regression balancing exploration and exploitation over feature vectors

hypotheses.statement: Learners allocated to KT-guided adaptive policies (Arms 1, 2, 3) will achieve significantly higher normalized learning gains (Hake's g) on post-assessment compared to control (Arm 0).
Dueling Double DQN (Arm 2) will demonstrate superior exercise efficiency (mastery gain per exercise attempt) compared to rule-based baselines.
The Hysteretic Difficulty Recovery mechanism embedded in Composite Adaptive (Arm 1) will significantly lower learner frustration rates (episodes with >=3 consecutive failures) to below 5%.

stopping_rules_and_safety.adverse_pedagogical_clause: If any experimental arm demonstrates statistically significant negative learning gains compared to baseline at interim analysis (N=15 per arm), that arm will be immediately halted.
